Blocks 640, 641, 642, 643, 645, 646, 647, 648, 757, 758, 759, 760, 762, 763, 764, 765. Only the lyriq blocks state this value. gid1 8032, 8034, 8036, 8038, 9032, 9034, 9036 and 9038 on 302-220 and 313-340 are in no other source as a gid1: Google's rules, AOSP's carrier list and Samsung's rules do not list them. Samsung's IMS data has 8032 to 8036 and 9032 to 9036 only as gid2 under gid1 8030 and 9030, and 8038 and 9038 nowhere. So nothing shows that a SIM reports these digits as gid1, and Motorola's list may hold gid2 values in the gid1 place. The profiles are unnamed and have no recorded source family. findings.effect: allow_hold_call_during_emergency_bool (CarrierConfigManager.java:2509-2516, default true at :12089). With false, TelephonyConnectionService hangs up every other TelephonyConnection and conference with cause OUTGOING_EMERGENCY_CALL_PLACED before it places the emergency call (TelephonyConnectionService.java:2392-2408; the same in recreateEmergencyConnection at 3545-3559; read at 3704-3714). Telecom's CallSequencingController also disconnects a managed ongoing call whose account carries false (CallSequencingController.java:1016-1037, 1097-1100); CallsManager.java:4623-4647 fills a missing key with true. The hangup marks the ImsPhoneCall DISCONNECTING (ImsPhoneCall.java:251-260), which is not alive (Call.java:53-55), so checkForDialIssues and prepareForDialing go straight to the dial (ImsPhoneCallTracker.java:2716-2734, 1648-1697). With true the tracker first holds the active call, and prepareForDialing throws 'cannot dial in current state' if that hold fails (1683-1689); a live foreground and background call stop the dial with ERROR_TOO_MANY_CALLS (2730-2733). No other reader of the key exists in the telephony, Telecom, IMS framework or ImsStack sources, the ocd fork included, so no TTY, RTT or priority path reads it. The cited files are the same on lineage-24.0. On a phone: a group A value is admitted only for the most specific profile that sets the key, else the Google-lane value, else Android's default (Serving.kt:405-440).
findings.risk: None from holding: Android's default true stays. If such SIMs exist they keep the hold-first path every phone without carrier data has.
